subject: Latitude Systems onboarding timeline, commitments & acceptance checkpoints

Date: Mon, 7 Oct 2029 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Draft MAP & kickoff timing for Latitude Systems

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, I put together a concise mutual action plan (MAP) sketch so we can lock down roles, milestone dates, and acceptance criteria before the formal kickoff. Key points:

- 0-14 days: Provisioning and network validation (customer VPC peering, firewall rules) — Owner: Latitude (Paul) + Redwood infra (Jonas).
- 15-45 days: Model onboarding and integration testing (API keys, test prompts, KV cache validation) — Owner: Redwood CS (Marissa) + Latitude integration engineer.
- 46-90 days: Performance tuning and capacity reservation; go/no-go acceptance for production traffic — Owner: Redwood SRE (Mina) + Latitude ops.

I attached a spreadsheet (Latitude_MAP_v1.xlsx) with a proposed calendar and acceptance checks. Can you confirm availability for a 30-minute kickoff this Thursday (10/10) at 11am PT? If that works I’ll loop in Marissa and Jonas to start the milestone owners list.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Ben —

Really appreciate the quick turnaround and clear milestones. A couple of notes from our side before the kickoff:

1) Our security team requested an example of the audit logs export and the expected retention window (SOC2-related).
2) For the 15-45 day integration phase, can Redwood provide a lightweight test harness or sample prompts for our engineering team to run against staging?
3) On capacity: we’d like a temporary burst capacity for the first 2 weeks of production ramp to handle unpredictable traffic spikes. Can that be included in the commit?

Thursday 10/10 at 11am PT works for me and I’ll have Paul on. Please add the Redwood CS and SRE folks to cover the details above.

Best,
Aisha

Subject: Mutual action plan (version 1) — milestones, owners, and acceptance checks

Hi all —

Following Ben’s note, I pulled together a cleaned-up MAP (see attached: Latitude_MAP_v1.xlsx) and summarized the key milestones below. This is intended to be the operational checklist we track in the first 90 days; I’ll maintain the doc and update weekly during the cadence calls.

Milestone 1 — Provision & networking (Days 0–7)- Owner: Latitude (Paul) / Redwood Infra (Jonas)- Deliverables: VPC peering established, firewall rules applied, sample request returns 200 from staging- Acceptance: successful 3-run smoke test from Latitude IPs; timestamped logs available in shared Drive

Milestone 2 — Auth & API integration (Days 8–21)- Owner: Latitude eng / Redwood CS (Marissa)- Deliverables: API key exchange, SDK integration, sample prompt runbook- Acceptance: automated test harness (attached) passes 95% of baseline checks; integration ticket closed in Jira (LAT-102)

Milestone 3 — Load validation & tuning (Days 22–60)- Owner: Redwood SRE (Mina) / Latitude ops- Deliverables: staged load tests, recommended batching config, KV cache baseline- Acceptance: median P95 latency < 220ms on target payload, no data-plane errors > 0.1% during test window

Milestone 4 — Production ramp & SLA handoff (Days 61–90)- Owner: Joint ops (Latitude + Redwood)- Deliverables: capacity reservation, runbook for rollbacks, post-launch monitoring dashboard- Acceptance: production ramp to 100% with zero critical incidents for 72 hours; agreed runbook signed-off in the Drive doc

Open items we’ll cover Thursday:
- Security: sample audit logs export (Jonas/Mina to demonstrate)
- Burst capacity: Mina to propose temporary burst tier and cost estimate
- Escalation contacts: Redwood and Latitude on-call roster (please add your on-call emails in the doc)

Attachments: Latitude_MAP_v1.xlsx (milestones & calendar), test-harness-readme.txt (sample prompt harness), Latency-SLA-narrative.pdf

I’ll take action to create the weekly cadence invite (30 minutes) and a shared Jira board with the initial tickets. Please review the MAP before the call and flag any timeline concerns.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Marissa/Ben —

This looks good and very pragmatic — thank you. Two quick confirmations:

1) We’ll upload our firewall ranges and the contact for networking (Paul) to the shared Drive by EOD Wednesday (10/9).
2) We accept the proposed timeline but request the burst capacity window for Days 61–75 (first two weeks of production). If Mina can send the cost estimate before the kickoff we’ll review it live.

We’ll be on the kickoff Thursday at 11am PT. Looking forward to the weekly cadence — please send the calendar invite and Jira board link.

Best,
Aisha
Director of Platform Operations
Latitude Systems
